sprint: Image Studio gains a compose side panel: the cutouts a child ticks open in their own workspace beside the picture, where each one can be moved, resized and bucket-filled — and nothing touches the picture being edited until they tap 'Use This Picture'.
task:
THE ASK, verbatim: 'to draw a composite image open a side panel. this way the orignal edit is not lost.' The previous ship's Make One Picture shelf-packed the ticked cutouts and immediately overwrote the picture on screen — one shot, no arranging, and the edit underneath it gone. Now Make One Picture opens js/composePanel.js (window.ComposePanel) as a flex sibling of the stage, and the destructive apply runs only from its own Use This Picture button.

SHIPPED IN FIVE COMMITS, one per stage, each syntax-checked before the next: skeleton (c0ab42c) -> wiring (55198ad) -> paint + drag (0808573) -> scale, fill and the bake (0a79e3d) -> a real bug the suite caught (5b345a0).

DEPENDENCIES ARE HANDED OVER, NEVER REACHED FOR. configure({mount, tileEditor, onUsePicture}) at boot, mirroring the contextPanel/objectStrip host-binding convention, so composePanel.js never touches pictureStudio.js's closure. PngEncoder is a BARE global in this codebase (never window.PngEncoder — see the sheet extractor's own call sites), so its typeof guard matters: a missing script tag is a silent ReferenceError at call time, a repeat failure mode here. It was dropped again at Stage 6 once it turned out to be configured, stored and never read — _applyComposedPicture takes the raw buffer straight into _swapWorkingBuffer, so no PNG is ever encoded; the header and configure() comments that claimed otherwise are corrected rather than left to mislead the next reader.

PAINTING keys a per-tile offscreen canvas cache on the pixel-buffer OBJECT rather than an index, which is what lets a drag redraw every frame without re-uploading anything; the cache is dropped in both open() and close(), since a stale entry could never be mis-read (the keys are distinct identities) but every one of those canvases is real memory nobody can reach again. Hit testing walks tiles topmost-first and is ALPHA-AWARE — after the bbox reject it reads the source pixel's own alpha byte, so tapping the hole in a ring falls through to whatever is behind it instead of grabbing the ring's box. Pointer coordinates convert through getBoundingClientRect because the canvas lays out at width:100%;height:auto.

SCALE is about the tile's own TOP-LEFT — the corner _tileRect() measures from and _surfaceSize() grows around — so a growing tile pushes the surface out and x/y stay non-negative with no extra clamping.

FILL WAS WRITTEN BUT UNREACHABLE: _fillTile read _state.fillPoint, which nothing ever wrote, so its guard returned every time. The pointerdown handler already had the canvas-space point in hand and was dropping it, so it is passed as an argument rather than smuggled through a state field that exists for one call.

THE BAKE composites by hand in a raw Uint8ClampedArray and NEVER through a canvas readback, because a canvas backing store is premultiplied and mangles RGB wherever alpha is partial — which is exactly what a cutout's edges are made of. Sampling is nearest-neighbour on purpose: bilinear would invent partial alpha along every edge and soften the boundaries the extractor worked to keep clean. At the default scale of 1 the mapping is exactly 1:1 and nothing is resampled. The preview uses drawImage and so reads slightly smoother than the bake at other scales — disclosed in the comment rather than papered over.

ONE REAL APP BUG, FOUND BY THE SUITE RATHER THAN BY INSPECTION: every fill came out pure black. TileEditor.bucketFill indexes col[0..2] straight into the output buffer; handed the hex string '#ff00ff' it wrote the CHARACTERS '#','f','f', each coerced to NaN and then stored as 0 by the clamped array — so the call succeeded, the tile repainted, and the result was silently wrong. hexToRgb lives in tileEditor.js but is NOT on its export list, so the fix carries its own converter, the same per-module adapter convention js/pictureStudio.js already follows for this exact call.

VERIFIED 71/71, zero page errors, via compose_panel_verify.mjs (scratch-only, self-hosting server on a dynamic port). Sections: A (17) panel structure, lazy DOM, scoped .hidden rules and the button-cascade overrides; B (6) open/close/isOpen and idempotency; C (6) shelf-pack layout and surface growth; D (11) drag, alpha-aware hit testing, clamping, and the Move/Fill mode switch — D6/D7/D8 are the fill checks that caught the bug; E (15) scale about top-left, fill on a copy, and the bake's own pixel content — E8 is the fill check; F (6) Use This Picture end to end, including that the panel auto-closes through _toggleActiveTool's existing hook rather than a close call of its own; G (8) teardown across both routes (leaving the tool, and _hide(), since a modal dismissal never routes through _toggleActiveTool — close() is idempotent, so the overlap is harmless); H (2) zero page errors.

THE ERROR COLLECTOR WAS SPLIT rather than loosened: genuine pageerrors are separated from failing-resource console noise, the ignored set is cross-checked against a KNOWN_BAD list and PRINTED, so the filter cannot quietly grow to cover a real problem. Confirmed the ignored set is exactly the four documented entries — Story Egg's hero.png/magic.png/personality.json and the sandbox's Supabase block.

Full regression: both goldenBuild suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. renderer/slideRenderer.js is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Cache-bust ?v=0362 -> ?v=0363 across all 60 tags. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — tools/world-builder/, tools/world-builder-v2/ and tools/sheet-extractor/ are completely untouched; confined to a new js/composePanel.js plus js/pictureStudio.js, css/style.css and index.html.
